positions.commentary: The speaker expresses enjoyment of the earnings update and believes the company successfully balanced a long-term view with latest news.
The speaker notes that Google had great earnings, announced a dividend, and the stock is up 12-15% today, but remains concerned about META's partnership.

thesis: The episode argues that Meta is executing a successful turnaround driven by strong user growth, improved ad targeting via AI, and a return to free cash flow conversion, despite heavy investments in Reality Labs and the Metaverse. The speaker views these high expenses as a necessary investment cycle with clear monetizable opportunities, though the timing of when this investment phase will end remains uncertain. Conversely, the episode suggests a bearish view on Google due to competitive concerns arising from Meta's AI partnerships.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that META's free cash flow has converted and is expected to improve as CAPEX approaches DNA, with LTM free cash flow estimated at $34 billion.
claims.quote: And so 2023, it was 74% LTM, it is still 74%. And so you do see that that free cash flow started to convert, which is what you want to see. And the reason why, though, it is below 100% and will continue to be below below 100% for the foreseeable future is because CAPEX has been running much higher than DNA.

claims.claim: The speaker highlights that META's daily active people reached an all-time high of 3.24 billion, indicating strong user growth across their apps.
claims.quote: Even though people are calling for the imminent demise of Facebook, et cetera, we don't have Facebook usage stats broken out specifically, but we do know daily active people reached an all-time high of 3.24 billion. So that is most of the entire world's internet population is on one of their apps.

claims.claim: The speaker states that META's ad impressions grew 20% year over year, driven by relevant and targeted ads that users enjoy seeing.
claims.quote: And so the third one is going to be ad load. This is within meta's control to an extent. They can't place as many ads as they want within the feed. However, the amount of ads that they can place in the feed has been much higher than many people would have ever expected. And this is in part because the ads are so relevant and targeted that people actually enjoy seeing them.

claims.claim: The speaker mentions that META's stock price is $440, up from $30 when the reverse DCF was originally cut, indicating a significant increase in valuation.
claims.quote: And one way alternatively of thinking about the ad pricing is you can kind of just think about it as the amount of ad targeting that is going to happen. And so the way that kind of works mentally is that if you're assuming a flat return on ad spend, then any targeting improvement is bid back up into the same ad price.

claims.claim: The speaker discusses META's partnership with Google and Bing to bring real-time information into their large language model, noting that it is very early.
claims.quote: And then Mark Zuckerberg said, oh, it's very early. But yeah, we could definitely see how we could put some ads into that chat box. And I was like, whoa, wait a minute, wait a minute, wait a minute. That seems not great for Google.

claims.claim: The speaker expresses concern about META's partnership with Google, suggesting it could be bad for Google if everyone has their own chat interface.
claims.quote: And I know we've talked about this at ad nauseum and Speedwell doesn't technically cover Google. But, what do you think about that? I mean, if there's a world where everyone has their own little chap, I'm on an Instagram and I pull up, hey, what is this? I mean, that seems like a really bad world for Google.

claims.claim: Meta demonstrated a dramatic turnaround with significant revenue growth and operating leverage in 1Q24.
claims.quote: In 1Q24, it was a continuation of that theme. We saw that revenue grew 27% against expenses of just 6%. And so again, this is part of the year of efficiency, continuing on.

claims.claim: Meta's AI initiatives are driving improvements in ad targeting and recommendation systems.
claims.quote: And so that is the thing that we're saying now. They do give impressions in ad pricing data, which impressions grew 20% and ad prices grew 6%, which you would prefer to see impressions actually growing rather than ad pricing.

claims.claim: Meta's AI recommendation systems are now serving a significant portion of content in Facebook and Instagram feeds.
claims.quote: And so they gave some numbers that now 30% of the Facebook feed is AI recommendations and 50% of the Instagram feed is now AI recommendations.

claims.claim: Meta is aggressively investing in AI infrastructure, increasing its CAPEX guidance.
claims.quote: And in fact, they actually up their CAPX guidance. Now they're talking about doing 30 to 37 billion in CAPEX, a $2 billion increase on the high end from prior.
